'''Claes Fahlander''' (born 21 January 1948 in [[Gothenburg]]) is a Swedish [[physicist]]. As of May 2025, he is [[Professor Emeritus]], Particle and Nuclear Physics, at [[Lund University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Claes Fahlander |url=https://portal.research.lu.se/en/persons/claes-fahlander |access-date=2025-05-09 |website=Lund University |language=en-GB}}</ref> 

After completing studies at [[Gävle University College]] in 1967, he attended [[Uppsala University]], where he obtained his [[bachelor's degree]] in [[mathematics]] and [[physics]] in 1972. He became a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in [[nuclear physics]] in 1977,  and a teacher in 1982. Between 1979 and 1982 he worked at the [[Australian National University]] in [[Canberra]], and in the following decade at Uppsala University. During a 1995 to 1997 [[sabbatical]], he was a researcher at the Laboratori Nazionali di Legnaro in [[Italy]],<ref>{{Cite news |title=Valbopojken väljer ut Nobelpristagarna |last=Larsson |first=Kristian |work=Absolutnu! |publisher=Sorrento |year=2006 |page=6 |language=Swedish}}</ref> and on 1 July 1996 he succeeded [[Hans Ryde]] as professor of Cosmic and Subatomic Physics at Department of Physics at [[Lund University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.kva.se/sv/nyheter/nya-ledamoter-i-fysikklassen|title=Kungl. Vetenskapsakademien|website=www.kva.se|date=12 January 2006 |access-date=2017-06-01}}</ref>

Fahlanders’ research has focused on studies of the shape of the [[atomic nucleus]], its core patterns and electromagnetic properties, as well as forces between [[proton]]s and [[neutron]]s in nuclear nuclei.<ref name=":0" /> In 2016, Fahlanders and his team verified the discovery of [[element 115]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sydsvenskan.se/2016-05-24/pa-fysicum-lever-drommen-om-lundium---lunds-eget-supertunga-grundamne|title=Atomjägarna spårar nya, supertunga grundämnen|work=Sydsvenskan|access-date=2017-06-01|language=sv-SE}}</ref> which had previously been discovered in [[Dubna, Russia]] in 2003.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/news/element-115-one-step-closer-to-periodic-table/|title=Element 115 one step closer to periodic table|access-date=2017-06-01|language=en}}</ref>

Fahlander was elected as a member of the Royal Physiographic Society in [[Lund]] in 1998 and as a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in 2006.<ref name=":0" />
